name: Question 4
problem:
$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,\text{_______},\,(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(x,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [-2,2].$ What is the second component of $r?$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/56a380b075d10862170ed9c9a45c07dddff3eaef1ea9fb3109a61cc3d27b5ac4.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [a,b]$ has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(x)=4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}\ge 0$ for all $x\in [-2,2].$ 

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [-2,2],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

  

Therefore, the second component of $r$ is $(4{x}^{2}-{x}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

Question 4

r(x,θ)=⟨x,_______,(4x2−x4)sin⁡θ⟩

The vector-valued function r(x,θ) above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve y=4x2−x4 by 2π radians about the x-axis for x∈[−2,2]. What is the second component of r?

a
4x2cos⁡θ
b
πx4sin⁡θ
c
2π(4x2−x4)cos⁡θ
d
(2x−x2)sin⁡θ
e
(4x2−x4)cos⁡θ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A point (x,y,z) on the surface generated by rotating the graph of y=f(x) by 2π radians about the x-axis for x∈[a,b] has the position vector

r=⟨x,f(x)cos⁡θ,f(x)sin⁡θ⟩,x∈[a,b],θ∈[0,2π).

First, notice that y=f(x)=4x2−x4≥0 for all x∈[−2,2].

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

r(x,θ)=⟨x,(4x2−x4)cos⁡θ,(4x2−x4)sin⁡θ⟩,x∈[−2,2],θ∈[0,2π).

Therefore, the second component of r is (4x2−x4)cos⁡θ.
